items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: And Joe Watkins to this day still talks of Japan. He and Manny Sales and I bummed around together sometimes if we had an off evening and explored the little bars and pubs and they just loved it.

ctx.x: It's hard to imagine that happening in any city in the world. Yeah. So, what did George think of Japan? Did you ever hear him talking about it?

He loved it. He loved it. He loved the people of, I think the words that he, one of the records, George Lewis in Japan, his closing salutation to them or saying goodbye to them, I think it's completely honest, the lovely people of Japan. He was so pleased. He recognized fully their appreciation of what he was doing. Yes. And he responded to it. And all the musicians do. And Joe Watkins to this day still talks of Japan. He and Manny Sales and I bummed around together sometimes if we had an off evening and explored…

I think it's a great question. Let's, let's, let's, we can perhaps change the subject a little. Um, George's funeral was on Friday and you were not only there but playing in one of the bands. And perhaps you can, I mean this is, we're fairly close to this right now but you know in years of time people will want to know about the funeral I think. Perhaps you can say something about it and, uh, as you brought back in. The general, just describe what happened.
